title: CrossCodeEval: A Diverse and Multilingual Benchmark for Cross-File Code Completion
note: Full text; benchmark paper - BM25/UniXCoder/ada embedding retrieval of fixed 10-line raw code fragments (top-5, ≤512 tokens), EM/ES/identifier-F1 vs in-file-only and oracle-reference baselines, budget not explicitly held constant across retrieval methods.

title: RepoHyper: Search-Expand-Refine on Semantic Graphs for Repository-Level Code Completion
note: Full text; Repo-level Semantic Graph is a call/import/class-hierarchy dependency graph (no control/data-flow edges), Expand-and-Refine graph retrieval with link prediction, outperforms baselines with quantified accuracy, budget-matching not stated.

title: GraphCoder: Enhancing Repository-Level Code Completion via Code Context Graph-based Retrieval and Language Model
note: Abstract only; Code Context Graph explicitly encodes control-flow and data/control-dependence between statements, coarse-to-fine graph-guided retrieval, quantified EM/identifier-match gains (+6.06/+6.23) vs RAG baselines, no explicit budget matching.

title: M2rc-Eval: Massively Multilingual Repository-level Code Completion Evaluation
note: Full text; benchmark paper - model input is in-file text plus Jaccard-similarity-retrieved cross-file line fragments (max 4096 tokens); AST used only to label completion points/buckets, not as model input; compares in-file-only vs +retrieval, not a strict budget-matched design.

title: Knowledge Graph Based Repository-Level Code Generation
note: Full text; AST-derived Neo4j knowledge graph (class/method/function/attribute nodes) combined with full-text+embedding entry search, n-hop graph traversal, and re-ranking - genuinely hybrid graph+retrieval. Pass@1 vs baselines on EvoCodeBench (20.73% vs 17.45%/7.27%), authors explicitly do not control for context length across conditions.

title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
note: Abstract only; studies SWE-agent/OpenHands tool-output/observation history; coded mechanism as fixed/recency-window masking (the paper's central finding is that simply omitting older observations matches LLM summarization) - genuinely contests summarization/learned_pruning, and proposed hybrid; quantified cost/solve-rate on SWE-bench Verified, not budget-matched a priori (cost is the measured outcome).

title: SpareCodeSearch: Searching for Code Context When You Have No Spare GPU
note: Abstract only (html/pdf full text unavailable); GPU-free keyword/lexical retrieval (no dense embeddings) of code chunks, evaluated via chrF (0.748 Kotlin, 0.725 Python) on Code Context Competition leaderboard - quantified but budget-matching vs other competition entries unconfirmed.

title: Stingy Context: 18:1 Hierarchical Code Compression for LLM Auto-Coding
note: Full text (PDF); TREEFRAG builds a hierarchical metadata tree (name/category/type/tagline/description per function-level node), 18:1-24:1 compression vs raw code; beats flat-chunking/RAG/AST/call-graph/GraphRAG baselines in blinded task ranking (22/40 tasks) but budget is not held constant (compression is the manipulated variable). Note: single-author, patent-pending, self-published venue - quality/credibility concerns.

title: When Retrieval Hurts Code Completion: A Diagnostic Study of Stale Repository Context
note: Full text; oracle-controlled diagnostic manipulation of stale-vs-current raw function-signature snippets (emulates but is not a real retriever) across current-only/stale-only/no-retrieval/mixed conditions on 17 curated samples; NOT budget-matched (mixed condition adds more content); quantified induced-staleness rates (up to 88.2pp) across 2 models.

title: Antaeus: Hunting Repository-Level Logic Vulnerabilities via Context-Grounded LLM Reasoning
note: Full text; hybrid of Tree-sitter-derived call/dependency graph + a repo-wide LLM-generated semantic summary bundle (trust boundaries/actors/protected objects) + function-level raw code, with static-analysis/keyword prioritization (149,758->4,859 functions) funneled into agentic LLM ranking; compared vs function-level and agentic baselines on 28 repos, no budget-matched ablation (cost/depth differ across methods).

title: SWE-Pruner Pro: The Coder LLM Already Knows What to Prune
note: Abstract only; a small trained head reads the coding agent's own internal representations to make keep-or-prune decisions per line of tool-output/observation text; up to 39% token savings, +3.8% SWE-bench Verified resolve rate across 2 backbones/4 benchmarks, not budget-matched (savings vary by condition rather than being fixed).

title: Paritok-4B: Intent-Conditioned Context Compression for Coding Agents
note: Abstract only; 4B LoRA model (Qwen3-4B) extractively/intent-conditionally selects spans from agent trajectory tool-outputs/file-reads, distilled from OpenHands trajectories; compared vs gpt-4.1-mini/gpt-5 compressors on compression ratio (25.7%) and SWE-bench Lite solve-quality retention (86.5%), not budget-matched to a common target size; extractive span-selection also arguably fits learned_pruning.
